Thanks again for the time yesterday. Two things we promised to follow up on related to your concerns about how prefix/prefetch hits are attributed and when StellarNet would be charged:

1) A concise explanation of our accounting model for cached prompt state (what counts as a billable token on a cache hit vs exempt).
2) A short proposal for a trial credit and a suggested contract tweak that addresses your compliance team’s requirement for clear, measurable billing rules.

Quick context from your note: you want to ensure that repeated invocations that match a cached prefix (including optional metadata) are not double-billed in ways that pop the unit economics during pilot. You also asked whether generated prefixes (server-side templating) vs user-supplied prefixes are treated the same.

Attached I’ve included our latest ratecard (redwood-ratecard-v3.pdf) for line items and a request that you share a small sample of real prompt events — that will let us run exact examples. If you prefer, Karthik can map a few of your rows to the billing model and show a per-call breakdown.

Proposed next steps:
- If you share a 24–48 hour sample of prompt events we’ll produce a labeled example mapping (no charge).
- We’re prepared to include a pilot credit of 10,000 billed-token credits to offset early-stage measurement noise while we agree final wording.

Would you be okay sharing a CSV extract? If procurement needs legal wording up front, we can propose a short clause that codifies the attribution rule; Karthik included suggested language in cc.

Thanks —

Hi Maria — thanks for the sample. I pulled a couple of rows and sketched a reproducible rule below so your legal team can evaluate. High level — we aim to make billing deterministic and easy to test.

Suggested attribution model (short form):
- A cache hit is considered "prefix-preserving" and is NOT billed for the prefix tokens if, at the time of request, the cached KV-prefix exactly matches the sequence of tokens used as the prefix for generation, including whitespace and any client-visible metadata fields that influence tokenization.
- When any client-visible field that affects tokenization differs between the stored cache entry and the incoming request (even if semantically similar), the request is billed for the full token sequence used to compute the model output.
- Server-side templating is considered a client-visible input for billing purposes if it is applied as a deterministic token sequence that is part of the encoded prompt. If you version your template and reference a template-id in the call, identical template-id + identical tokenized template => eligible for prefix exemption.

Example mapping (from your csv):
- Row A: template-id=welcome_v2, user_body="What is the status?" => 14 token prefix + 5 token body. If an identical stored cache exists for welcome_v2 with the same tokenization, the 14 prefix tokens are not billed on a hit.
- Row B: template applied inline as generated text that changed spacing => mismatch -> entire sequence billed.

Contract language stub (one sentence):
"Redwood will not charge for prefix tokens on a cached hit where the request’s tokenized prefix sequence exactly matches the stored cache entry for the same template-id (if provided) or exact token sequence otherwise; differences in any client-visible field that affect tokenization invalidate the exemption."

Credit proposal: we propose 10,000 billed-token credits to cover the pilot window while the teams validate attribution (applies only to billed-token metric; not to non-billable audit logs). We can increase to 25,000 if StellarNet commits to a three-month pilot with a minimum monthly consumption target.

I’m happy to produce a per-row billing spreadsheet showing line-by-line billed vs exempt tokens for a handful of sample rows — will share that shortly.

Cheers,
Karthik
